description: Given a list of integers a and a non-negative integer x with 1 <= x < length of a, return a pair (m, p). m is the maximum of the first x elements of a: every one of a[0..x-1] is at most m and m equals one of them. p is meant to be the index of the first element at position x or later that is strictly greater than m, or the last index of a if there is no such element. Precisely, p must satisfy x <= p < length of a; if p is not the last index then every element before position p is strictly smaller than a[p]; and if no element at position x or later is greater than m then p is the last index.
notes: Translated as in VERINA, whose conditions on p are weaker than the description (they do not force p to be the first element after position x that exceeds m). VERINA's 'exists i < x, a[i] = m' is written in Dafny with the recursive predicate OccursInPrefix (with a {:fuel} hint) because the verifier cannot decide membership in the slice a[..x] on concrete lists; Python uses 'm in a[:x]'.
